source.title: Memorisation Cartography: Mapping out the Memorisation-Generalisation Continuum in Neural Machine Translation
source.authors: Verna Dankers; Ivan Titov; Dieuwke Hupkes

record.tranche_reason: The study measures training memorisation and generalisation scores for NMT examples, then tests how removing map regions changes held-out performance. It uses a different memorisation measure and task than the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study’s own results relate example-level counterfactual memorisation to NMT held-out performance. Feature correlations and MLP prediction scores are not separate rows because they do not test a listed version. The study does not test the claim versions as specified.
record.test_reason: The study reports related NMT results but does not test any listed version. Its closest connection is V8: it removes regions defined by counterfactual memorisation and measures translation performance. It does not compare removing the most memorised examples against removing equally many random examples, or measure image-classification accuracy. Its counterfactual memorisation metric is adapted from the same inclusion-based concept as V8; the metric's provenance is not the reason for exclusion.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that high-CM examples generally contribute most to NMT performance, with the most beneficial map region depending on the metric. Such examples can also introduce vulnerabilities: evaluated high-CM training examples are more associated with perturbation-induced hallucinations. They additionally show that surface features can approximate memorisation scores and caution that memorisation is multidimensional.
record.recipe_differences: Uses counterfactual memorisation scores and NMT translation metrics; does not test random-label fitting, width, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or the stated influence-ranked ResNet example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: The association between high-CM examples and hallucinations differs by training setting: it is reported for §6.1 models trained on those examples, but not for §6.2 models trained on other examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing NMT map regions with higher counterfactual memorisation generally harms held-out BLEU and target log-probability more than removing low-CM regions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High-counterfactual-memorisation training regions contribute disproportionately to held-out translation performance in this EN-NL Transformer setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Training on regions selected using predicted memorisation scores produces some metric-specific improvements over token-matched random training data, with the largest relative improvement in hallucination tendency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Predicted memorisation-map positions can guide NMT data selection for particular performance metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: High-CM regions can help reduce overall hallucination tendency, while high-CM evaluated examples are more associated with elicited hallucinations when models trained on those examples; that association is not reported for §6.2 models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relation between counterfactual memorisation and perturbation-induced NMT hallucinations depends on the training and evaluation setting.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The performance-impact and specialised-training results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The study uses one language pair for the performance analysis, selected regions and three seeds per subset; the authors note that the setup uses a smaller dataset than state-of-the-art NMT and does not investigate major changes such as model size or larger datasets.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance under matched architectures and training recipes.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed to fit the training set.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialisation.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and their dependence on tuning or weight decay.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalisation-gap rankings, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.

Test-accuracy losses from removing the most memorised image-classification examples versus equally many random examples. NMT region removal supplies related evidence but does not test this comparison.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions because every row measures an unlisted effect; this does not negate the study's stated qualitative findings. Figure values cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text. No listed-version results requiring additional rows were found.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out comparisons and tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout effects and its interactions with data augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.

The study removes groups of NMT examples by counterfactual memorisation-map region, not examples ranked by the stated influence-based criterion; it measures BLEU, target log-probability, and hallucination tendency rather than ResNet test accuracy on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet.
